blue-catfish: Upper Chesapeake Bay Cooper Goff holds up a large blue catfish he caught in the Conowingo Dam pool.
Blue catfish are in play this week and can be found from the Conowingo Dam pool south to all the region’s tidal rivers.
This is an excellent time of the year to catch blue catfish and pack fillets in your freezer for the winter.
largemouth-bass: Largemouth bass and crappie will start to hold in deeper waters near structure.
Largemouth bass are holding in deeper waters as November progresses, and they will be ready to grab any baitfish or crayfish attempting to move to deeper waters.
If targeting structure, wacky rigged stick worms or similar soft plastics can entice a largemouth bass to pick up a bait.
smallmouth-bass: Coldwater fish such as smallmouth bass, walleye, trout, and chain pickerel do well in cooler waters.
Fishing for smallmouth bass and walleye is good this week in Deep Creek Lake and the upper Potomac.
Smallmouth bass can also be found in Liberty and Prettyboy reservoirs.
striped-bass: Striped bass activity along these channel edges can be revealed by diving seagulls as striped bass push schools of bait towards the surface.
Jigging with soft plastic or metal jigs is the most popular way to fish for striped bass this week.
There is still shallow-water action for striped bass being reported by anglers this week.
walleye: Coldwater fish such as smallmouth bass, walleye, trout, and chain pickerel do well in cooler waters.
Fishing for smallmouth bass and walleye is good this week in Deep Creek Lake and the upper Potomac.
Walleye can be found along steep rocky shores of Deep Creek Lake during the evening hours and working jerkbaits along the deeper edges is a good way to target them.
white-perch: White perch are being found in the lower sections of the region’s tidal rivers and holding in deep waters over oyster beds and other types of structure.
Middle Bay Rich Watts caught this large white perch while jigging deep at the Bay Bridge recently.
The Kent Narrows should not be overlooked for striped bass or white perch.

access.note: NPS Point of Rocks Boat Ramp, 3703 Canal Rd, Point of Rocks MD 21777, C&O Canal mile 48.2; auto and boat-trailer parking, vault toilet. C&O Canal Trust also notes a small lot at the train station for day and overnight use.

rules.text: Nontidal waters (MD), statewide: harvest 01-01–12-31 15 in minimum 5 per day / 10 possession
Potomac River mainstem, nontidal (MD): harvest 01-01–04-15 15-20 in slot 5 per day / 10 possession; 04-16–12-31 15 in minimum 5 per day / 10 possession
Maryland-Virginia boundary is the low-water mark on the Virginia shore; Maryland owns the riverbed (Black-Jenkins award 1877). Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virginia_v._Maryland

NPS: Maryland license required for 16+ in nontidal waters; regs follow the state where you fish. Fishing from the Virginia bank would be a separate question. Source: https://www.nps.gov/choh/planyourvisit/fishing.htm
License: Maryland nontidal license (Matt's stated license; not verified here) (per Matt; not verified)

rig.primary: 3/8 oz round jighead (2/0) with 3.5-4 in white or chartreuse paddletail/grub, 20 lb braid to 3 ft 12 lb fluoro
rig.alternate: Suspending jerkbait 4.5 in (silver/black or clown) or small shallow crankbait, 20 lb braid to 3 ft 12 lb fluoro, #1 round snap
rig.switch_trigger: Snagging every cast in rock, or fish seen chasing near the surface at dusk
rig.gear_note: Workable on Matt's 7 ft Crossfire MH (20 lb braid) with the leader dropped to 10-12 lb; ideal is a 6'6"-7' medium spinning rod with 10 lb braid. The unconfirmed 6'6" Ugly Stik fits if the 17 lb leader is swapped lighter.
